plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, often fragrant, double or single blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply lobed leaves. It is a classic cottage garden favorite and thrives in climates with cold winters.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live for more than 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A hardy, suckering shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and rough, dark green foliage. It is one of the oldest cultivated roses and a parent of many modern garden roses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (late May to June)
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally for centuries and retains its fragrance when dried.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they fall. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics it blooms in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; cultivated in Southern California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, thousands of trees line the streets, and in some places falling blossoms are said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with white petals around a bright yellow center, growing in meadows, roadsides, and grasslands. It forms clumps of upright stems with lobed, dark green leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized throughout North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Each oxeye daisy flower head is actually a composite of many tiny flowers: the white 'petals' are ray florets and the yellow center is made up of disc florets.
